questions.q: What kind of operations does the Azure Activity Log / AWS CloudTrail Event history track by default?
options: Control-plane operations — creating, updating, and deleting resources — not data-plane operations like reading a row or an object
Only data-plane operations, like reading individual rows or objects
Only billing events
Only failed login attempts
questions.explain: Both logs are, by default, control-plane audit logs: a record of management operations on resources. Data-plane logging is separate and opt-in in both clouds.

questions.q: In the Azure Activity Log, what does it mean when the 'Event initiated by' column shows 'Microsoft Azure Policy Insights' instead of a person?
options: An Azure Policy effect (such as DeployIfNotExists) actually fired and made the change automatically, not a human
The log entry is corrupted and should be ignored
A person named 'Policy Insights' made the change
The event happened before Azure Policy existed
questions.explain: This is a direct, visible trace of an automated Azure Policy effect taking action, distinct from a manual change made by a person.

questions.q: What does the Azure Activity Log's 'Change history' feature show, for operations that support it?
options: The actual before and after values of specific properties around an event, such as a VM's power state changing
A list of every user who has ever logged into the subscription
The billing cost of the operation
Only the operation name, with no additional detail
questions.explain: Change history captures property-level before/after values tied to a specific event, going beyond just logging that an operation happened.

questions.q: How long does CloudTrail's Event history retain management events by default?
options: The last 90 days, for the current AWS Region
Indefinitely, with no retention limit
7 days
Only the current calendar day
questions.explain: Event history is a rolling 90-day window by default — the same default retention period as the Azure Activity Log.

questions.q: Why do most production environments configure a CloudTrail 'trail' or export Azure's Activity Log to a Log Analytics workspace?
options: Because the default 90-day retention window is usually shorter than what compliance or investigation needs require
Because the default logs are not accurate and need to be re-verified
Because the default logs only capture failed operations
Because exporting is required before any log entries are generated at all
questions.explain: The 90-day default is enough for routine troubleshooting but short of most compliance retention requirements, so exporting to longer-term storage is near-universal in production.
